Nyirmihalydi Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírmihálydi, Hungary

Not demolished. The older of two Jewish cemeteries in Nyírmihálydi, appearing on an 1870 cadastral map with tombstones through 1914. First recorded with 9 residents in the 1747 census, the community formally organized in the second half of the 19th century, joining the Orthodox stream and Balkány's larger jurisdiction in 1885; population peaked at 137 by 1880, declining sharply as youth emigrated after WWI. Young men were conscripted for forced labor at the end of 1942; by 1944, only 43 Jews remained before the community's dissolution and deportation from Harangod-puszta to Auschwitz on May 20 that year. Just 3 Jewish residents remained per the 1949 census.
